data.narrative:
Copenhagen Atomics is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $25M+. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across the nuclear energy sector: three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy universe—only one direct same-stage peer was identified, below the three-datapoint threshold required for reliable cross-sectional benchmarking. Consequently, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $25M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $50M.

The triangulated range spans $42M (low) to $57M (high), with a median of $50M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single quantitative method rather than true triangulation across approaches. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for this early-stage, capital-intensive sector and the absence of contemporaneous private transaction data for nuclear-focused peers at equivalent stages. A more robust valuation would benefit from additional comparable transactions or cash-flow-based methods as the company matures and benchmarking data becomes available.
